content.value_statement: Frontend teams need reusable components with clear APIs, consistent styling, and accessible behavior. This skill guides React, Vue, and Svelte patterns for component libraries and design systems.
actual_capabilities: Explains compound components, render props, slots, and controlled versus uncontrolled patterns.
Shows React, Vue, and Svelte examples for reusable component architecture.
Compares CSS Modules, Tailwind CSS, styled-components, Emotion, and Vanilla Extract.
Covers ARIA roles, keyboard handling, focus traps, live regions, and form errors.
Discusses theming, code splitting, and critical CSS extraction for component libraries.
Provides guidance for prop naming, variants, slots, and style overrides.
limitations: Focuses on component architecture, not full app routing or backend behavior.
Examples require adaptation to project conventions and dependencies.
Accessibility guidance still needs manual testing with keyboards and assistive tools.
Does not execute build tools, install packages, or validate bundle output.

use_cases.title: Build Design System Components
use_cases.description: Create shared buttons, tabs, forms, and overlays with consistent APIs and accessibility behavior.

use_cases.title: Refactor Framework Components
use_cases.description: Move legacy React, Vue, or Svelte components toward composition patterns and simpler prop contracts.

use_cases.title: Select Styling Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare CSS Modules, Tailwind, styled-components, Emotion, and Vanilla Extract before standardizing a UI stack.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for reusable UI parts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain component composition choices for a reusable button, card, and modal in my React app. Recommend clear props and accessibility checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Component API
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component API for a design system. Identify prop conflicts, composition opportunities, and naming changes for long-term reuse.

prompt_templates.title: Design Compound Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a compound component pattern for tabs with controlled and uncontrolled usage. Include accessibility states and framework tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Framework Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-framework component library for React, Vue, and Svelte. Compare styling strategy, theming, API consistency, and migration risk.

output_examples.input: I need a reusable dropdown menu for a design system.
output: Recommends trigger, menu, and item parts with shared state.
Defines keyboard behavior for Escape, arrow keys, Home, and End.
Flags focus return and outside-click handling as required behavior.

output_examples.input: My button has too many visual props.
output: Groups visual states into variants and sizes.
Suggests composition for icons and loading content.
Keeps accessibility props available through normal button attributes.

output_examples.input: We need one styling approach for a new component library.
output: Compares runtime cost, server rendering, theming, and learning curve.
Matches CSS Modules, Tailwind, Emotion, styled-components, and Vanilla Extract to project needs.

best_practices: Start with semantic HTML, keyboard behavior, and ARIA only where it adds meaning.
Prefer composition when a prop list becomes difficult to document or test.
Keep styling tokens and component states consistent across frameworks.
anti_patterns: Do not add props for every visual exception before checking composition.
Avoid copying examples without matching your project dependencies and browser targets.
Do not treat CSS-in-JS or utility classes as substitutes for API design.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React, Vue, and Svelte component patterns with shared design system concerns.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples that can guide implementation. Review and adapt them for your stack.

faq.question: Does it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes ARIA roles, keyboard handling, focus management, live regions, and form error patterns.

faq.question: Can it choose a styling library?
faq.answer: It compares common options and helps select one based on runtime cost, theming, and team needs.

faq.question: Can it review an existing component?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to assess props, composition, controlled state, accessibility behavior, and style boundaries.

faq.question: Does it focus on native Web Components?
faq.answer: No. It mainly focuses on framework UI components, not the Custom Elements API.
